description.narrative: MIFTAH – Outcome 3: Enhanced Institutional and Social ResilienceMIFTAH will lead Outcome 3, focusing on strengthening institutionaland social resilience at the community and local governance levels. Drawing on its expertise in community empowerment, social accountability, and inclusive governance, MIFTAH will support community-based disaster risk reduction (DRR), social cohesion, and accountable local governance. The interventions will prioritize the meaningful participation of women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other marginalized groups, reinforcing resilience, trust, and inclusive decision-making.Output 3.1: Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR)MIFTAH will establish 14 inclusive community DRR groups, ensuring the participation of women, youth, elderly people, and persons with disabilities. At least 170 community members (minimum 50% women) will be trained in shock-responsive planning, riskanalysis, and preparedness. These groups will develop and implement 14 community DRR plans and practical initiatives, strengtheninglocal capacity to anticipate, respond to, and recover from climate, environmental, and socio-economic shocks.Output 3.2: Community Cohesion and Social AccountabilityTo strengthen social cohesion and inclusive participation, MIFTAH will train 28 community members (at least 50% women) on feedback, complaints, and protection mechanisms. Fourteen community-led social cohesion initiatives will be implemented to promote dialogue, trust-building, and collective action within and between communities.Output 3.3: Local Government Unit (LGU) Governance and AccountabilityMIFTAH will strengthen local governance by training 170 LGU staff (at least 20% women) on inclusive decision-making, good governance principles, and social accountability. A transformative leadership development programme will be delivered to selected LGU representatives. In addition, two social accountability mechanisms per community will be implemented,alongside 14 governance initiatives, to improve transparency, inclusive service delivery, and trust between communities and local authorities.

participating-org.narrative: MIFTAH was founded in December 1998 under the leadership of Dr. Hanan Ashrawi with the support of prominent Palestinians from different fields serving on its boards of directors and trustees. The organizations main aim is to participate in setting the foundation for the establishment of an independent Palestinian state that affords its citizens a decent life and enjoys the respect of the international community. MIFTAHs various activities with a focus on women and youth seek to change the culture, policyand legislations, which inhibit the participation and influence of different marginalized groups. Key elements of MIFTAHs work aim to build a sound foundation of good governance by conducting extensive work in breaking down the barriers hindering the participation of the marginalized groups in the Palestinian society. Core programs focus on supporting womens participation in elections including successful lobbying to afford them some representation by law. In the past MIFTAH sponsored women candidates andsupported them through training for elections. MIFTAH also focuses on the youth and women through leadership training, and works with marginalized localities to build their planning capacities. In addition to work on good governance, MIFTAH works to disseminate the Palestinian narrative through an active web site and the hosting of numerous briefings to foreign diplomats and delegations, both officials and non-governmental visiting OPT.
